To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prognostic value in non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) of the C-reactive protein (a marker of inflammation), measured before chemotherapy, is underestimated by the conventional proportional hazard (PH)-model, and that flexible modeling shows that the hazard associated with high CRPs is highest in the first 18 months after diagnosis, and then declines.

flexible modeling improves assessment of the prognostic value and timing of C-reactive Protein (CRP) in non-small cell lung Cancer (NSCLC), which has implications for patient management and clinical trials.
the Cox's PH regression model underestimates the prognostic value and the time frame of C-reactive proteins in non-small cell lung cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of flexible modeling to improve prognostic assessment in advanced cancer patients.
the development of a flexible model that allows for non-proportional hazards and nonlinear effects of prognostic factors in survival analysis, while adjusting for multiple prognostic variables.
the value of CRPs in predicting survival in NSCLC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
high CRP is an independent prognostic factor for NSCLC patients, and that the association of CRP and mortality is non-linear and time-varying.
high CRP is associated with a worse prognosis in NSCLC, but the association is not linear and the effect is not stable throughout the follow-up period.
CRP is a strong independent prognostic factor for mortality in NSCLC, with an early effect that lasts for about 18 months, and a later effect that lasts for at least 24 months. © 2015 The Authors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cox's PH analysis is not the best way to assess the prognostic value and time-dependent nature of a biomarker.
the flexible modeling provides a more accurate and complete assessment of the value of CRPs as a prognosticator for survival in NSCLC.
CRP is a useful biomarker in NSCLC, but that it should be measured as close as possible to the initiation of treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
flexible modeling is an important tool in evaluating the role of prognostic factors in clinical trials.
flexible modeling can improve the prognostic assessment of CRP and that the prognostic value is not limited to advanced NSCLC.
flexible modeling can provide a better assessment of the prognostic value, and thus the clinical utility, of CRP in NSCLC.
